results.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 complete English document plus CSV/JSON exports
results.coverage: front matter pp.1-22, chapters V1-V17 pp.23-95, appendices A-E pp.96-119; all 345 requirement IDs checked
supported: three verification levels L1/L2/L3 with 70/183/92 requirements
unconfirmed: trust-boundary framing: zero occurrences of trust boundary across PDF, CSV, JSON and source markdown
results.conclusion: The leveled clause is supported and three of four framing clauses are supported, but the trust-boundary clause is not present. The conjunction is not fully supported.

results.revision: Final, 17 February 2026; 21 numbered sections plus appendices A-B
results.evidence: Section 11.4 Revocation states that the specification does not define a revocation process.
results.nuance: Key revocation status fields exist in 8.7.2-8.7.3 and trust-mark revoked status in 8.4.2, but no revocation process is defined.
results.conclusion: The removed claim is contradicted by the specification's own Section 11.4.
results.resolution: Split the claim. The process clause is contradicted; revocation status data for keys and trust marks is supported.

results.source: Google SRE Workbook, all content chapters and appendices
results.coverage: forewords, preface, Parts I-III, chapters 1-21, appendices A-C, index, editors, colophon; all 34 content pages read
results.evidence: Evernote uses an external prober outside the environment, multiple geographic locations and a second prober to confirm failures; Chapter 2 describes browser probes and a browser home-page SLI; Chapter 5 describes synthetic user activity and coverage limits. The exact definition and the explicit-design rule are absent.
results.conclusion: Clause-level support exists for external probing, locations, false positives, browser probes and artificial activity; the exact synthetic-monitoring definition and design rule remain unconfirmed. Reclassified under R-01.

results.source: Enterprise Integration Patterns book; public pattern pages are publisher-abridged
results.coverage: All cited public pages read; Chapter 3 PDF read. Chapters 4+ are withheld from the public site. A controlled-lending copy exists at archive.org/details/enterpriseintegr0000hohp but was not borrowed, so the full text was not obtained.
results.conclusion: Each conjunction is split into supported and unconfirmed clauses; the original conjunction is not fully supported and the full Chapter 4+ text remains unavailable. Reclassified under R-03.

results.coverage: complete served page; publisher-abridged after the mechanics paragraph
results.evidence: The page says to attach the Routing Slip specifying the sequence of steps to each message and to read it at each step. It does not use variant, encode or path wording, and the full book text is withheld.
results.conclusion: Core mechanism is supported by the served page; complete-source confirmation is not available.

results.source: PostgreSQL 18.6 Continuous Archiving and PITR page

results.evidence: The page covers recovery targets, base-backup retention and WAL retention, but never states RPO, RTO or restore verification as determinants.

results.source: Enterprise Integration Patterns, Chapter 3 Messaging Systems, author-hosted PDF
results.coverage: complete chapter, all 42 pages; Pipes and Filters pp.70-77
results.evidence: p.72 attributes buffering to channels; p.74 says concurrency can reorder messages; p.77 says the simple filter is not transactional. These support the concerns but do not demonstrate the universal every-stage wording.
results.conclusion: The universal claim is not supported; clause-level support exists. Reclassified under R-02.
